question: In a 24-year-old presenting with dystonia and behavioural change, serum ceruloplasmin alone is sufficient to rule out Wilson's disease if it is within the normal laboratory reference range.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. A normal ceruloplasmin does not exclude Wilson's disease. Ceruloplasmin is an acute-phase reactant and can be falsely elevated in Wilson's patients with concurrent inflammation. In any patient under 50 with an unexplained movement disorder, full Wilson's disease workup — including 24-hour urine copper and KF ring slit-lamp exam — is mandatory.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct that this is FALSE. Ceruloplasmin can be falsely normal in up to 5–20% of Wilson's disease patients (it is an acute-phase reactant and may be elevated by concurrent inflammation). A normal ceruloplasmin does NOT exclude Wilson's disease. The diagnostic workup requires 24-hour urine copper, slit-lamp examination for Kayser-Fleischer rings, and often liver biopsy or ATP7B gene sequencing.
